title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This sits in the 'Teichmüller tower' notes (c. 1978-81). Grothendieck works with the profinite fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4} = P^1 - {0,1,∞}, taken at a finite S_3-stable set of base points, and with the anharmonic S_3-action. The figure on the previous page is an S_3-equivariant cell decomposition of the sphere with these vertices:
- P^± (one per half-plane ω = ±): presumably the order-3 fixed points e^{±iπ/3}, i.e. the j = 0 orbifold point.
- Q_0, Q_1, Q_∞: presumably the order-2 fixed points -1, 2, 1/2, i.e. j = 1728.
- R_i^ω (six of them): points near the punctures i in each half-plane, plausibly tangential.

The edges come in three packets a_i^ω, c_i^ω, d_i^ω, each an S_3-torsor. The relations (48) are a pentagon-like cycle d^{-1} c^{-1} a^{-1} c d = 1 (with permuted indices). Each vertex group is identified with Π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1 - 3 points) by isomorphisms φ_i^ω (at R), ψ_i^ω (at Q) and ψ̃_i^ω (at P). These are tied together by the edges (51). The standard automorphisms of Π_{0,3} that enter are σ_∞ (an involution), ε_0 and ρ (order 3).

This page.
- (53) records how transport along a_i^ω twists φ_i^ω by ε_0.
- He then parametrizes endomorphisms u of the profinite groupoid that fix all vertices and commute with S_3. By S_3-equivariance such a u is determined by its values on one representative of each edge packet, subject to (48). Since an endomorphism changes an edge by a vertex-group element, one gets (54): u(a) = a·φ(λ), u(c) = φ(η)·c = c·ψ(η), u(d) = ψ(ζ)·d = d·ψ̃(ζ), with three parameters λ, η, ζ ∈ Π̂_{0,3}.
- Rather than expand (48) by brute force, he uses a van Kampen-type argument. The groupoid is covered by two sub-groupoids II and IV (labels from the decomposition) whose intersection is III. So an equivariant endomorphism amounts to: an endomorphism (λ, η) of II plus an endomorphism ζ of IV that induce the same endomorphism α̃ of III.
- This gives the two expressions (55): α̃ = η^{-1} ε_0(λη) and α̃ = ζ ρ^{-1}(ζ^{-1}).

Next page. He eliminates α̃, getting the single relation (56) η^{-1} ε_0(λη) = ξ ρ^{-1}(ξ)^{-1}. He then changes variables (β = σ_∞(η)η^{-1}, α = σ_∞(λ)β, ...) to reach a 'familiar' form.

Purpose. This is a hands-on computation of the 'Teichmüller-type' symmetry monoid at the level of M_{0,4} with its S_3 symmetry: the order-2 and order-3 relations. It is the content later packaged as Drinfeld's two- and three-cycle relations for GT-hat (1990).

Geometric reading. M_{0,4}/S_3 is the j-line, so the vertices P and Q are the orbifold points of orders 3 and 2. The II ∪ IV decomposition is in effect a van Kampen computation for an orbifold groupoid, the same mechanism behind PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3.
errors: Cannot fully verify (53)-(55) without the precise edge conventions. Since τ(a_i^ω) = (a_i^{ω'})^{-1} on the previous page suggests a_i^ω joins R_i^ω to R_i^{ω'}, (53) as written, with φ_i^ω on both sides, looks index-inconsistent. One side may need ω' or index ωi; this could be a slip of notation.

The claim that the parameters are subject only to the relation deduced from (48) presupposes that II and IV are connected and that van Kampen applies to the profinite completions of the sub-groupoids. This is true for these free and orbifold groupoids but is left implicit.
The second expression in (54) (c·ψ_0^ω(η)) has subscript 0 where ψ_i^ω would be expected. This is probably a notational slip or a misreading.

ideas.what: Parametrizing S_3-equivariant, vertex-fixing endomorphisms of the profinite fundamental groupoid of M_{0,4} at several S_3-special base points by elements (λ, η, ζ) of Π̂_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: GT-type description of Out/End of the genus-0 Teichmüller groupoid at the 4-point level; precursor of Drinfeld's GT-hat
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §2, announces in general terms the determination of the tower's automorphisms by the M_{0,4}/M_{1,1} and M_{0,5}/M_{1,2} levels, without these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Using a covering of the groupoid by sub-groupoids II and IV with intersection III (van Kampen gluing) to turn the edge relations into a single compatibility equation (55)/(56)
ideas.modern_name: van Kampen theorem for fundamental groupoids / orbifold decomposition of M_{0,4}/S_3 (j-line with orbifold points of order 2 and 3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brown (groupoid van Kampen); the use for GT is implicit in Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura–Schneps

ideas.what: Choosing base points at the S_3-orbifold points (order 3: P^±, order 2: Q_i) as well as near the punctures (R_i^ω)
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid with base points at elliptic points / tangential base points; link to M_{1,1} via M_{0,4}/S_3

missed.claim: An explicit pre-Drinfeld derivation of a GT-type relation, of the form η^{-1}ε_0(λη) = ζρ^{-1}(ζ^{-1}). It comes from S_3-equivariant endomorphisms of the M_{0,4} groupoid with base points at the orbifold points, and the setting is the endomorphism monoid rather than only the automorphism group. The archive manuscript documents how Grothendieck actually computed this, which is absent from the published Esquisse.
missed.quote: La donnée d'un endomorphisme des profinis groupoïdes, fixant les sommets et qui commute à S_3, équivaut à celle des transformés des a_i^ω, c_i^ω, d_i^ω ... (55) α̃ = η^{-1}ε_0(λη) et α̃ = ζρ^{-1}(ζ^{-1})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical value for priority on GT-hat. Its parametrization by three group elements, with base points at the orbifold points, may offer an alternative presentation of GT-hat or of its endomorphism monoid that is worth comparing with Drinfeld's (λ, f).

deep.surprise_reason: It is known that Grothendieck anticipated GT-hat. This page shows a concrete, specific computation route (S_3-equivariant groupoid, van Kampen gluing over II ∪ IV) that is not in his published texts. The underlying mathematics, however, is now standard.
transcription_corrections: In (54) and in the preceding sentence the edges are c_i^ω (as on the previous page), not b_i^ω.
Third line of (54): the right-hand side is d_i^ω ψ̃_i^ω(ζ) (tilde-psi, consistent with (50)), not φ̃.
The parameter is written ζ on this page (λ, ζ, η ∈ Π̂_{0,3}); the next page writes ξ for the same quantity.
'groupoïde univ.' is uncertain: possibly 'groupoïde envisagé' or 'universel'.
Marginal label (55) appears at bottom left next to 'à la fois'.
